paragraphs: Tower Hamlets Council runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies shown above also take enquiries from people in the borough. Fostering for the council means caring for Tower Hamlets children with the council's social workers supporting you; an agency assesses and supervises its own carers and takes children placed with it by councils. Enquiries to the council start with Local Community Fostering, the recruitment service it set up in May 2024 with Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, Newham and Redbridge. It passes enquiries to each council's own fostering team; the council's 2024/25 report notes that two boroughs left the partnership from May 2025 and that being part of it improved the council's conversion rate from enquiry.

When the service launched, the councils said London had about four children needing a foster home for every approved carer, and that approved fostering households in the capital had fallen from 3,685 in 2014 to 2,560 by March 2023. Locally, the Corporate Parenting Board's annual report for 2024/25 records 284 children looked after by the council at the end of March 2025, up from 276 a year earlier. Most were older children: 92 were aged 10 to 15 and 99 were 16 or 17, so carers for teenagers matter as much as carers for young children.

The same report sets out what the council offers its carers: 74 trainer-led courses with 806 places during 2024, a foundations course that 104 foster carers have now completed, three Mockingbird groups with a fourth planned, an independent foster carers' association that has run for about 20 years, and a buddy scheme being piloted for newly approved carers. The council's fostering service is Family Friendly accredited and offers allowances, support around the clock and training. From the 2026-27 financial year its foster carers pay no council tax: a 100% reduction, reimbursed at the end of a carer's first year of approval and paid on top of the fostering allowances.

Each October the council celebrates its foster and kinship carers; in 2025 nearly 100 were recognised, some of whom have fostered for more than 20 years. We do not yet have a Tower Hamlets allowance page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above what they pay and how they support carers of teenagers. The Newham, Hackney and London pages list more services nearby.
